steps: 1. Identify the discrepancy between the documented condition in the clinical note and the billed ICD-10-CM code.
2. Review the full clinical progress note to determine onset, etiology, laterality, and episode of care (initial, subsequent, sequela).
3. Cross-reference official FY 2024 ICD-10-CM Tabular List and Index for the correct diagnostic code.
4. Prepare a coding correction ticket documenting the chart excerpt and revised code rationale.
5. Void original unadjudicated claim or submit an EDI 837P replacement claim (Claim Frequency Code 7) with corrected ICD-10.
6. Document the resolution in the billing ledger and verify payer acceptance via 277CA.
1. Identify the unspecified diagnosis code on the claim line.
2. Inspect the complete medical record, including past medical history, lab results (e.g., eGFR, HbA1c), and physical exam.
3. Identify the highest level of clinical specificity documented by the attending provider.
4. Replace the unspecified code with the specific primary code and secondary manifestation codes as required by FY 2024 guidelines.
5. Transmit a corrected electronic claim (EDI 837P Type of Bill / Frequency 7) to the health plan.
6. Close the internal audit query and update coder educational log.
1. Review the clinical service rendered against the billed CPT code definition.
2. Check patient billing history to confirm patient status (new patient: no professional services within 3 years; established patient: seen within 3 years).
3. Select the correct CPT code reflecting actual encounter status and clinical work performed.
4. Recalculate Chargemaster gross charge and contractual allowance based on fee schedule.
5. Submit corrected claim with corrected CPT code.
6. Reconcile accounts receivable balance.
1. Inspect the claim lines for identical CPT codes, date of service, and provider.
2. Verify whether multiple independent procedures were clinically performed (which would require Modifier 59/XS) or if a clerical duplication occurred.
3. Confirm from operative/diagnostic report that only a single procedure was executed.
4. Void/cancel the duplicate service line in the practice management system.
5. Post a full credit/adjustment for the duplicate gross charge ($0.00 patient balance).
6. If payer already paid duplicate in error, initiate voluntary refund/takeback reconciliation.
1. Review the progress note against AMA/CMS 2021/2023 E/M documentation guidelines for Medical Decision Making (MDM).
2. Evaluate the 3 MDM elements: Number and complexity of problems addressed, amount/complexity of data reviewed, and risk of complications/morbidity.
3. Determine the supported E/M level (e.g., downcoding from Level 5 to Level 3).
4. Issue a formal coding notification to the rendering clinician explaining the downcoding rationale.
5. Submit a corrected claim reflecting the supported E/M code (e.g., 99213) and revised charge.
6. Update provider education dashboard.
1. Flag the unauthenticated progress note in the billing pre-scrubber workqueue.
2. Place an immediate billing hold on the encounter to prevent premature transmission.
3. Route an urgent EHR chart completion notification to the rendering provider.
4. Provider reviews, authenticates, and applies compliant electronic signature with timestamp.
5. Validate that chart status shifts from 'Draft' to 'Signed / Finalized'.
6. Release the billing hold and transmit the clean EDI 837P claim to clearinghouse.
required_evidence: EHR audit log with signature timestamp
Medicare Program Integrity Manual MLN MM6698

steps: 1. Review encounter charge ledger against EHR document repository.
2. Confirm that the billed procedural code (e.g., CPT 11102) has no documented procedure note or pathology report.
3. Place a strict billing hold on the claim.
4. Issue an official Provider Query to the attending physician requesting missing documentation.
5. If provider provides signed late entry with clinical justification, attach note and release claim.
6. If provider confirms procedure was not performed or cannot be substantiated, delete the charge from the billing ledger.
1. Review the clearinghouse EDI 277CA rejection report (STC: A7 / CARC 16).
2. Contact patient/parent guarantor to obtain correct subscriber ID, policy number, and employer group.
3. Update practice management Master Patient Index (MPI) with parent as primary subscriber and minor as dependent.
4. Re-execute real-time eligibility verification (EDI 270/271) to confirm active coverage.
5. Regenerate clean ANSI ASC X12N 837P claim file with valid Loop 2000B/2010BA data.
6. Transmit to clearinghouse and monitor 277CA acknowledgment.
1. Retrieve the clearinghouse demographic mismatch rejection notice (CARC 31).
2. Compare practice management registration data with patient intake form and driver's license / birth record.
3. Identify the typographical error (e.g., transposed month and day in DOB).
4. Correct the date of birth in the Master Patient Index and payer master record.
5. Re-run real-time eligibility check (EDI 270/271) to ensure match with payer database.
6. Resubmit corrected claim to clearinghouse.
1. Identify the HMO specialist visit denied under CARC 197 / RARC N381.
2. Check if a valid referral was issued by the Primary Care Physician (PCP) prior to the visit but not linked to the appointment.
3. If referral exists in external health system portal, retrieve referral number and attach to claim.
4. If no referral was issued, submit an urgent retroactive referral request to the PCP office with clinical consultation notes.
5. If retroactive referral is approved, resubmit claim with referral authorization number in Loop 2300.
6. If referral is definitively denied, write off the charge per in-network HMO contract rules (patient held harmless; zero balance billing).
1. Inspect Local Coverage Determination (LCD) policy for the billed procedure code.
2. Review the clinical progress note to identify whether symptoms or clinical indications were documented but not coded.
3. If clinical symptoms (e.g., dyspnea, abnormal auscultation) were documented, update diagnosis coding to include the covered indication.
4. If no medical necessity indication exists and the service was purely routine screening without documented clinical basis, hold billing for compliance officer review.
5. If confirmed non-covered and no Advance Beneficiary Notice (ABN) was signed prior to service, write off the charge. Patient cannot be billed.
6. Educate clinical staff on pre-ordering coverage checks.
1. Review the NCCI bundling denial (CARC 97) for the Evaluation and Management service billed alongside minor surgery.
2. Inspect the clinical documentation to confirm if the E/M service addressed a significant, separately identifiable medical problem beyond normal pre/post-operative care.
3. Verify that the documented history, exam, and medical decision making for the separate condition stand alone.
4. Append Modifier -25 to the appropriate E/M CPT code (e.g., CPT 99214-25).
5. Submit a formal corrected claim or administrative appeal packet with supporting clinical documentation.
6. Track ERA 835 remittance for unbundled reimbursement.
required_evidence: NCCI Policy Manual Chapter 1 General Correct Coding Guidelines

steps: 1. Review the Medically Unlikely Edit (MUE) denial under CARC 151 / RARC N362.
2. Inspect the clinical infusion/administration record to verify start time, stop time, and total elapsed duration (e.g., 45 minutes).
3. Review CPT guidelines for code 96360 (initial hydration, 31 to 60 minutes = 1 unit).
4. Correct the billing charge line from 4 units to 1 unit.
5. Adjust the practice management charge ledger to reflect the single-unit retail charge ($130.00).
6. Transmit corrected claim to payer for adjudication.
required_evidence: Nursing flow sheet with infusion start/stop times

steps: 1. Review the CARC 22 denial indicating primary coverage under another plan.
2. Review patient age and Medicare entitlement status (patient turned 65; Medicare Part B is active primary).
3. Update payer hierarchy in the practice management system: Medicare Part B as Primary, BCBS as Secondary.
4. Format and transmit a primary electronic claim (EDI 837P) to Medicare Part B.
5. Await Medicare ERA 835 remittance advice.
6. Upon receipt of Medicare payment, cross over or submit secondary claim with primary ERA 835 CAS segments to BCBS for secondary cost-sharing payment.
1. Audit the patient account ledger against the payer Electronic Remittance Advice (ERA 835).
2. Calculate the correct cost-sharing waterfall: Contractual Allowed Amount minus Deductible applied minus Copay minus Coinsurance.
3. Identify calculation defect where practice management script billed patient $164.40 on an allowable fee of $112.00.
4. Calculate exact enforceable patient liability: $50.00 deductible + $12.40 coinsurance = $62.40.
5. Void the erroneous patient billing statement.
6. Issue an immediate ledger adjustment credit and generate a corrected itemized statement for $62.40 with written apology.
1. Review clearinghouse 277CA syntax report identifying missing Box 24J/33a rendering NPI.
2. Inspect practice management system provider dictionary and taxonomy lookup tables.
3. Re-link rendering clinician's Type 1 individual National Provider Identifier (NPI 1982736450).
4. Validate that Box 33 billing group NPI and Box 24J rendering NPI populate correctly in Loop 2310B.
5. Re-run claim through pre-submission scrubber to verify clean claim status.
6. Resubmit EDI 837P file to clearinghouse and confirm 277CA acceptance acknowledgment.
1. Review the internal audit threshold alert flagging high-level E/M code CPT 99215.
2. Conduct independent audit of clinical progress note for Medical Decision Making (MDM) and encounter duration.
3. Confirm documented acute life-threatening presentation (severe chest pain, diaphoresis, acute cardiac transfer) meeting High MDM criteria.
4. Confirm face-to-face physician time of 50 minutes strictly meets CPT 99215 threshold.
5. Conclude that CPT 99215 and associated diagnosis codes are fully supported by clinical documentation.
6. Document 'No Error Identified' in audit log, release claim for billing, and adjust automated audit query rules to avoid unnecessary alerts on acute cardiac encounters.
required_evidence: ECG tracing and emergency transfer record

steps: 1. Review compliance auditor finding regarding high-risk medication initiation without source records in EHR.
2. Inspect medical record to confirm that outside rheumatology consultation report and autoimmune lab panels are referenced in text but absent from media repository.
3. Place an interim billing hold on the encounter claim.
4. Task medical records / clinical assistant to contact external rheumatology facility to obtain formal consultation report and laboratory serologies.
5. Scan and index external records into the patient's EHR chart.
6. Re-evaluate documentation completeness; once verified, release claim for billing.
